name: Leukaemia
preview_text: The person with high fever and bleeding needs a very different herbal strategy than the person with profound fatigue and night sweats - TCM distinguishes these patterns and treats ...
conventional_description: Leukaemia is a cancer of the blood-forming tissues, including the bone marrow and lymphatic system. It leads to the overproduction of abnormal white blood cells, which crowd out healthy blood cells. This results in symptoms such as persistent fatigue, frequent infections, easy bruising or bleeding, bone pain, and unexplained fevers. Diagnosis typically involves blood tests, bone marrow biopsy, and genetic analysis to classify the type and guide treatment.
conventional_treatments: Conventional treatment depends on the type and aggressiveness of the leukaemia. It often includes chemotherapy, targeted therapy, radiation, immunotherapy, and in some cases, stem cell transplant. Supportive care such as blood transfusions and antibiotics is used to manage low blood counts and infections. The goal is to achieve remission by eliminating leukemic cells and restoring normal blood production.
tcm_understanding:
In TCM, leukaemia is understood as a deep-seated disorder of the bone marrow, which is governed by the Kidney system. The Kidneys store the body's essential life force, or Jing, and produce the marrow that creates blood.
When this system is damaged by inherited weakness, environmental toxins, or emotional strain, the marrow becomes a breeding ground for pathological heat and toxins. This is why the disease is often called "marrow toxin" or "blood cancer" in classical texts.
The Spleen and Stomach are also central. They transform food into Qi and Blood, the daily fuel that keeps the body warm and nourished. When the Spleen is weakened, the body cannot replenish its blood cells, leading to the pale complexion and crushing fatigue that are so common.
In some patterns, intense Toxic-Heat blazes through the blood, causing high fevers, bleeding gums, and purplish skin spots - a sign that the heat has penetrated the deepest level of the body and is forcing blood out of the vessels.
What makes TCM's view so different is that it sees each person's leukaemia as a unique landscape of excess and deficiency. One person may have blazing heat that needs to be cleared urgently, while another has a smouldering emptiness where the body's cooling Yin has been consumed, leaving a low-grade fever and night sweats. Still others have hard masses and stabbing bone pain from stagnant blood.
These patterns can shift and overlap, especially with chemotherapy, which often damages both Qi and Yin. Treatment is not one-size-fits-all - it adapts to the pattern that is active right now.
classical_translation: "The bone is the residence of the marrow; when the marrow is deficient, the bones will ache. This classical insight directly parallels the deep bone pain characteristic of leukaemia, where marrow pathology leads to pain."

tcm_diagnosis:
A TCM practitioner starts by asking about energy and complexion. If the person looks pale, feels deeply exhausted, and experiences dizziness or heart palpitations, the picture points toward Qi and Blood Deficiency. The tongue is often pale with a thin white coat, and the pulse feels thready and weak. This pattern is especially common in the chronic phase or after chemotherapy, when the bone marrow struggles to produce healthy blood.
When a sudden high fever, raging thirst, and bleeding gums or purplish skin spots appear, the practitioner suspects Toxic-Heat blazing in the blood. The tongue is red with a yellow coat, and the pulse is rapid and flooding. Questions focus on the intensity and timing of fever, any nosebleeds, or dark urine. This pattern signals a severe, acute crisis that demands urgent cooling of the blood.
If the person complains of lingering low-grade fevers that worsen in the afternoon, night sweats, and a dry mouth alongside persistent tiredness, the practitioner thinks of Qi and Yin Deficiency. The tongue may be pale or light red with a thin coat, and the pulse is thready and rapid. Here the exhaustion comes from a dual drain on both vital energy and cooling fluids, often seen during recovery or remission.
Empty-Heat caused by Yin Deficiency shares the night sweats and low fevers, but the heat signs are more pronounced: a sensation of heat in the palms, soles, and chest, a dry throat, and a red tongue with little or no coating. The pulse is thready and rapid. The practitioner distinguishes this from Qi and Yin Deficiency by noting that the fatigue is less overwhelming; the body’s cooling system is simply too dry to keep the fire in check.
When the abdomen feels full or a hard mass is felt under the ribs, accompanied by fixed bone pain or stubborn bruising, Blood Stagnation is likely. The tongue appears purplish with dark spots, and the pulse feels choppy or wiry. Palpation of the liver and spleen area and asking about the nature of pain-whether it is stabbing and fixed-help confirm that sluggish blood flow is complicating the underlying condition.

patterns.symptoms: ["Persistent, deep fatigue and lack of energy", "Pale or sallow yellowish complexion", "Dizziness or lightheadedness", "Heart palpitations", "Shortness of breath, especially on exertion", "Poor appetite or reduced food intake"]
patterns.worse_with: Overwork or physical exhaustion, Skipping meals or poor nutrition, Raw, cold, or iced foods and drinks, Emotional stress
patterns.better_with: Warm, nourishing meals, Rest and adequate sleep, Gentle exercise or movement, Calm, stress-free environment
patterns.why_this_happens: In leukaemia, the bone marrow becomes crowded with malignant cells, which directly damages its ability to produce healthy red blood cells and the Qi that circulates them. The Spleen, which transforms food into Qi and Blood, is often too weakened by the disease or treatments to compensate for this loss. The result is a deep, persistent state of Qi and Blood Deficiency, where the body lacks the vital energy and nourishment needed to function, leading to profound fatigue, pallor, and a range of other deficiency symptoms.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: pale body, may be thin or show teeth marks on the edges, with a thin white coating. Pulse: fine (thin) and weak, especially in the right Guan position (Spleen).
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work:
Qi and Blood are produced by the Spleen from the food we eat and the rest we take. Overwork, poor diet, and cold foods directly weaken the Spleen, draining the very resources the body is trying to build. This is why a leukaemia patient in a Qi and Blood Deficiency state feels worse after pushing through fatigue or eating a raw salad.

Warm, cooked foods and adequate rest support the Spleen's transformative function, making it easier to generate the Qi and Blood that are being lost. Gentle movement helps Qi circulate without depleting it, while a calm mind prevents the emotional knots that further stagnate and weaken the Spleen.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Focus on warm, easily digestible, nourishing foods like bone broths, congees, slow-cooked stews, dark leafy greens, and small amounts of high-quality protein. Avoid raw, cold, and iced foods which dampen the Spleen's ability to transform food into Qi and Blood. Prioritize gentle, restorative movement like walking or qigong, and ensure plenty of rest to allow the body to rebuild its reserves.

patterns.better_with: Cool, well-ventilated environment, Cooling foods and drinks, Light, bland foods like mung beans and pears, Rest and adequate sleep
patterns.why_this_happens: In leukaemia, external pathogenic toxins or internal imbalances generate intense Toxic-Heat that invades the bone marrow, the deepest level of the body. This blazing heat forces the blood out of the vessels, leading to bleeding gums, nosebleeds, and purplish skin spots. The heat also consumes the body's fluids, causing raging thirst and a dry, red tongue, while the struggle between the toxin and the body's defences produces a high fever.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: red or deep red body with prickly raised papillae and a dry yellow coating. Pulse: rapid (数 shuò) and forceful, often overflowing (洪 hóng) or full (实 shí).
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Toxic-Heat is a severe internal fire that rages upward and outward. Anything that adds heat-spicy food, anger, or hot surroundings-pours fuel on the flames, worsening the fever and bleeding. Cooling foods and environments, on the other hand, help the body clear the toxin, while rest conserves the Qi needed to fight the disease.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Keep the body cool with light, non-greasy foods like mung bean soup, cucumber, and watermelon. Avoid alcohol, coffee, lamb, and deep-fried or spicy dishes that add internal heat. Rest in a quiet, well-ventilated room and stay well hydrated with plain water or chrysanthemum tea.

patterns.why_this_happens: The leukemia itself and the treatments used to fight it, such as chemotherapy, can deeply drain the body's core energy (Qi) and its cooling, moistening fluids (Yin). When Qi is weak, you feel profoundly exhausted, short of breath, and have no appetite. When Yin is depleted, the body loses its ability to stay cool and hydrated, leading to a dry mouth, night sweats, and a lingering low-grade warmth, especially in the palms and chest.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: Red or pale-red body with a thin or absent coating, possibly cracked and dry. Pulse: Fine, weak, and often rapid.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Qi and Yin Deficiency means the body lacks the energy and fluids to function. Rest and nourishing foods help rebuild these reserves, while overexertion and drying habits deplete them further. A calm, cool environment prevents the mild heat from Yin deficiency from flaring up.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Focus on easily digestible, nourishing foods like congee, steamed vegetables, and bone broths. Avoid spicy, greasy, or overly hot foods that consume Yin. Gentle activities like walking or tai chi can help build Qi without depleting it. Prioritize rest and sleep to allow the body to recover.

patterns.why_this_happens: Yin is the body's cooling, moistening foundation. Leukaemia itself, along with chemotherapy and radiation, can deeply deplete Yin, leaving the body without enough substance to anchor the warmth of Yang. This creates a relative excess of heat that rises and disturbs the body, much like a kettle boiling dry. The result is low-grade fevers that come and go, night sweats, and a persistent dry, hot sensation in the palms, soles, and chest.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: red, thin, and dry, often with cracks and little or no coating. Pulse: fine (thin) and rapid, weak at the deep level.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: When Yin is depleted, the body lacks the cooling resources to balance its natural warmth. Anything that adds heat or consumes fluids-like spicy food, stress, or overwork-will make the empty heat flare up, causing more night sweats and fevers. Rest, hydration, and cooling foods gently replenish Yin and calm the fire, allowing the body to restore its natural equilibrium.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Focus on foods that build Yin and fluids: pears, watermelon, cucumber, tofu, black sesame, and congee. Sip water or chrysanthemum tea throughout the day. Avoid spicy, fried, or greasy foods that create more heat. Prioritize rest and sleep, and avoid late nights or overwork, which burn Yin. Gentle, non-sweaty movement like tai chi or walking is beneficial.

patterns.why_this_happens: In leukemia, the bone marrow is the birthplace of blood. When the disease process or its treatments create stagnation, the flow of blood becomes sluggish and obstructed. This leads to hard, fixed masses like an enlarged liver or spleen, and stabbing, knifelike bone pain that is worse at night and with pressure. The stagnant blood also fails to nourish the skin and tissues, causing a dark, dusky complexion and purplish spots (purpura) that do not fade.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: dark purple or dusky body with stasis spots, distended dark sublingual veins, and a thin white coat. Pulse: choppy (涩 sè), like a knife scraping bamboo, or wiry (弦 xián).
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Cold and inactivity cause blood to congeal and stagnate further, which is the root of this pattern. Warmth and gentle movement invigorate blood flow, helping to break up the stasis. Emotional stress tightens the Liver Qi, making it harder for blood to move smoothly, so calming the mind is essential.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Keep the body warm and avoid cold, raw foods and iced drinks, which congeal blood. Gentle daily movement like walking or tai chi helps keep blood circulating. Include warming, blood-moving foods such as turmeric, black fungus, and a little dark vinegar in cooking.

faqs.question: Can TCM be used alongside chemotherapy?
faqs.answer: Yes, TCM is often used as a supportive therapy during chemotherapy. Herbal formulas and acupuncture can help manage side effects like nausea, fatigue, and low blood counts. However, it is critical that your TCM practitioner and oncologist communicate. Some herbs may interact with chemotherapy drugs or affect liver enzymes, so never self-prescribe. Always bring a full list of your treatments to both practitioners.

faqs.question: How quickly can I expect to feel better?
faqs.answer: Improvement timelines vary by pattern and stage. In acute Toxic-Heat crises, cooling herbs can bring down fever and reduce bleeding within a few days. For the deep fatigue and night sweats of deficiency patterns, many people notice a lift in energy and better sleep within 2 to 4 weeks, but full rebuilding of Qi and Yin reserves typically takes several months of consistent treatment.

faqs.question: Are there any foods I should avoid?
faqs.answer: Generally, avoid spicy, greasy, and deep-fried foods that can generate internal heat and dampness. Raw and cold foods can weaken the Spleen and should be limited if you are already fatigued and have a poor appetite. Alcohol and smoking are strongly discouraged as they add toxic heat. A warm, easily digestible diet of soups, congees, and cooked vegetables is most supportive.

faqs.question: Can acupuncture help with bone pain?
faqs.answer: Yes, acupuncture can be very effective for bone pain, especially when the pain is fixed and stabbing, which suggests Blood Stagnation. Points like Xuehai SP-10 and Geshu BL-17 help move blood and relieve pain. Even in other patterns, acupuncture can calm the nervous system and reduce the perception of pain. Many patients find it a valuable non-drug option for comfort.

faqs.question: Will TCM cure my leukaemia?
faqs.answer: TCM is not a substitute for conventional cancer treatment. Its role is to strengthen the body, reduce side effects, improve quality of life, and support recovery. In some cases, it may help maintain remission and prevent relapse by correcting underlying imbalances. It works best as an integrated partner, not a replacement.

faqs.question: Is it safe to take herbs if my blood counts are low?
faqs.answer: Herbs can be used safely with low blood counts when prescribed by a qualified practitioner who understands your full medical picture. Certain herbs like Huang Qi (Astragalus) and Dang Gui (Angelica sinensis) are specifically used to support blood production. However, herbs that strongly move blood or cool heat may need to be avoided if platelets are dangerously low. Your practitioner will adjust the formula accordingly.

research.title: Dissection of mechanisms of Chinese medicinal formula Realgar-Indigo naturalis as an effective treatment for promyelocytic leukemia
research.description: This landmark study demonstrated that the traditional formula Realgar-Indigo naturalis, containing realgar, indigo naturalis, and salvia miltiorrhiza, exerts multi-target synergistic effects against acute promyelocytic leukemia. It provided a modern molecular explanation for the formula's clinical efficacy and spurred further research into TCM-derived therapies for leukaemia.
research.periodical: Wang L, Zhou GB, Liu P, et al. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. 2008.

research.title: Clinical observation on Qinghuang Powder in the treatment of chronic myelogenous leukemia
research.description: This clinical study observed that Qinghuang Powder, a classical formula containing indigo naturalis and realgar, achieved hematologic remission in a significant proportion of chronic myelogenous leukemia patients with relatively mild toxicity, supporting its use as a long-term maintenance therapy.
research.periodical: Zhou YX, et al. Chinese Journal of Integrative Medicine. 2005.
